### Computational Assignment Markdown

In this markdown, we analyse the provided ScanRecords.csv file and determine the unknown elements of the data.

```{r imports, echo=FALSE}
# first, need to import relevant packages and set the seed for our random processes
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

set.seed(333)

data <- read.csv("ScanRecords.csv")

# we convert the fraction of hours into minutes/hours in case we want to use it like this
# add the components we will need during our analysis (added retrospectively, further elaborated on later)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Minutes = (Duration * 60)
  )
data$PatientType <- as.factor(data$PatientType)
data

```

## Data Exploration

We have a few things we know about the data:

+ All series are independent and identically distributed
+ Patient 1:
    - The duration of scans are normally distributed
    - Patients arrive according to a Poisson distribution 

Let's first explore the data a little. Our focus is to find how the duration and arrival time are distributed, so we consider them first. 

# Durations

We start with the duration of scans.

```{r}
# look at how the duration of scans for each patient are spread
# use dplyr since it makes the data into a table dataframe automatically, makes it easier to work with
# for now use Minutes instead of Duration, but can switch it to Duration for equivalent results
dura <- data %>%
  group_by(PatientType) %>%
  summarise(
    SD = sd(Minutes),
    Max = max(Minutes),
    Qrt3 = quantile(Minutes, probs = 0.75),
    Mean = mean(Minutes),
    Qrt1 = quantile(Minutes, probs = 0.25),
    Min = min(Minutes)
  )
dura

# make the boxplot of the duration and the summary stats we find
boxDura <- ggplot(data, aes(x = PatientType, y = Minutes, fill = PatientType)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "MRI Scan Durations by Patient Type", 
       x = "Patient Type", 
       y = "Duration (minutes)") +
  stat_boxplot(geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(data$Duration)), by = 0.25)) +
  theme_minimal()

# want to visualise the statistics together with the boxplot, so use the gridExtra package to place them together
tdura <- t(dura)
duraVisual <- tableGrob(tdura)

grid.arrange(boxDura, duraVisual, ncol = 2, widths = c(2, 1.35))



```
The dots are outliers, which here are categorised as being more than 1.5 times the interquartile range above the third quartile, or below the first quartile.

# Arrivals

We can now look at the arrivals.
Because the time between arrivals is exponentially distributed (Poisson), we have to make a new column with the inter-arrival times. We have 21 days * 9 working hours per day, so so should have a total of 189 working hours. 
To find an accurate measure of inter-arrival time, we need to make the time in the data continuous (so that it flows from one day to the next). We can do that by making 

```{r}
# look at how many of each patient arrive each day
dailyCount <- table(data$Date, data$PatientType)
print(dailyCount)

# now find the inter-arrival times for each patient type separately
# for each arrival, group by patient type so that the inter-arrival times make sense
arr1 <- data %>% 
  filter(PatientType == "Type 1") %>%
  arrange(Date, Time) %>%
  mutate(
    DayIndex = as.numeric(as.factor(Date)) - 1,
    ContinuousTime = (DayIndex * 9) + (Time - 8),
    InterArrivalTimeHours = ContinuousTime - lag(ContinuousTime), # find difference in fraction of hours
    InterArrivalTimeMinutes = round(InterArrivalTimeHours * 60) # convert hour gap to minute gap 
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(InterArrivalTimeMinutes))

arr2 <- data %>% 
  filter(PatientType == "Type 2") %>%
  arrange(Date, Time) %>%
  mutate(
    DayIndex = as.numeric(as.factor(Date)) - 1,
    ContinuousTime = (DayIndex * 9) + (Time - 8),
    InterArrivalTimeHours = ContinuousTime - lag(ContinuousTime), # find difference in fraction of hours
    InterArrivalTimeMinutes = round(InterArrivalTimeHours * 60) # convert hour gap to minute gap
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(InterArrivalTimeMinutes))

summary(arr1)
summary(arr2)

```
Now we have the inter-arrival times for each patient type, so we can now look at how they are distributed visually.

```{r}
hist(arr1$InterArrivalTimeMinutes)
hist(arr2$InterArrivalTimeMinutes)
```



## Finding the Distributions - Bootstrapping

Now that we have the preliminary information, we can use this to find the distributions of the durations and arrival times for each patient using bootstrapping.

# Patient Type 1

As the case for Patient Type 1 is straight forward (we know the duration is normally distributed, and arrival is Poisson), we look at that first.
Have the sample mean and standard deviation, so use them as starting values to define the "true" distribution.

```{r}
# use the sample mean and standard deviation as baseline values
samplemu <- dura %>% 
  filter(PatientType == "Type 1") %>% 
  pull(Mean)  

samplesd <- dura %>% 
  filter(PatientType == "Type 1") %>% 
  pull(SD)  

# now prep for the bootstrap
# set the  number of runs and a matrix to hold the means for dura and arr
nlen <- length(data$Minutes)
B <- 10000
meansdura <- numeric(length = B) 
sdsdura <- numeric(length = B)

meansarr <- numeric(length = B) 

# now do a for loop where we do a bunch of normals to find the "true" mean
for (i in 1:B) {
  # generate normal based on params for duration
  samplebootdura <- rnorm(n = nlen, mean = samplemu, sd = samplesd)
  meansdura[i] <- mean(samplebootdura)
  sdsdura[i] <- sd(samplebootdura)
  
  # generate exponential based on params for arrival
#  samplebootarr <- rexp(n = nlen, rate = )
}

ci_lower <- quantile(meansdura, 0.025)
ci_upper <- quantile(meansdura, 0.975)

cat("Baseline Mean:", round(samplemu, 4), " with SD:", round(samplesd, 4),"\n")
cat("Bootstrap Mean:", round(mean(meansdura), 4)," with SD:", round(mean(sdsdura), 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI for : [", round(ci_lower, 4), ",", round(ci_upper, 4), "]\n")

# plot these to make it clear how the bootstrap and sample params interact
par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) 
# plot distribution of simulated means
hist(means, main = "Bootstrap Distribution: Mean", xlab = "Simulated Means (minutes)", col = "lightblue", border = "white")
abline(v = samplemu, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2) # Marks the baseline mean

# plot distribution of simulated standard deviations
hist(sds, main = "Bootstrap Distribution: SD",  xlab = "Simulated SDs (minutes)", col = "lightgreen", border = "white")
abline(v = samplesd, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2) # Marks the baseline SD
# Reset plotting layout to default
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
